title: English: Reported Speech
source: Written for Henry (Nov 17): direct → reported, reported → direct, tense backshift (past simple → past perfect etc.), rules. American spelling. Written answers show one model answer; other correct versions are fine (that is optional).

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Tom said, "I am tired."
Change to reported speech: Mia said, "I like this song."
questions.answer: Mia said (that) she liked that song.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: "We are playing soccer," the boys said.
questions.answer: The boys said (that) they were playing soccer.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Dad told me, "I will call you tomorrow."
questions.answer: Dad told me (that) he would call me the next day.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Anna said, "I have finished my homework."
questions.answer: Anna said (that) she had finished her homework.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: "I can swim," Ben said.
Change to reported speech: Lisa said, "I went to Phuket yesterday."
questions.answer: Lisa said (that) she had gone to Phuket the day before.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: The teacher said to us, "Open your books."
questions.answer: The teacher told us to open our books.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Mom said to me, "Don't be late."
questions.answer: Mom told me not to be late.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: "Where do you live?" Sam asked me.
questions.answer: Sam asked me where I lived.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Ploy asked me, "Do you like pizza?"
questions.answer: Ploy asked me if (whether) I liked pizza.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Nok said, "I am going to study here tonight."
questions.answer: Nok said (that) she was going to study there that night.

questions.q: Change to direct speech: He said (that) he was hungry.
Change to direct speech: She said (that) she had lost her phone.
questions.answer: She said, "I have lost my phone." (or "I lost my phone.")

questions.q: Change to direct speech: They said (that) they would come the next day.
Change to direct speech: Kim said (that) she could not find her keys.
questions.answer: Kim said, "I cannot find my keys."

questions.q: Change to direct speech: He said (that) he was reading a book then.
questions.answer: He said, "I am reading a book now."

questions.q: Change to direct speech: The doctor told me to rest.
Change to direct speech: She asked me where I lived.
questions.answer: She asked me, "Where do you live?"

questions.q: Change to direct speech: He asked me if I was ready.
Change to direct speech: Mom told us not to run.
Change to direct speech: Jim said (that) he had seen the movie the week before.
questions.answer: Jim said, "I saw the movie last week." (or "I have seen the movie.")

questions.q: "I live in Bangkok." She said she ___ in Bangkok.
"I am cooking." He said he ___.
Past simple → past perfect: "I broke my phone." He said he ___ his phone.
Past simple → past perfect: "We won the game." They said they ___ the game.
"I have finished." She said she ___ finished.
"I will help you." He said he ___ help me.
"I can speak French." She said she ___ speak French.
Past continuous → past perfect continuous: "I was sleeping." He said he ___.
"I must go now." He said he ___ go then.
"I have been waiting for an hour." She said she ___ for an hour.
"I am happy," she said. Which is correct?
choices: She said she has been happy.

questions.q: In reported speech, "tomorrow" usually becomes ___.
In reported speech, "yesterday" usually becomes ___.
In reported speech, "here" usually becomes ___.
The teacher ___ us to be quiet.
"Are you tired?" he asked. → He asked ___ I was tired.
"I have seen him." → She said she ___ him.
Which sentence is NOT correct?
choices: He asked me where I lived.
She said that she was busy.
He asked where did I live.
